ideal: It must be possible for a quantifier whose variable has a further condition to also have no fact for its variable beside another thing.
note: merged the two bullets into one sentence with "to also"

ideal: When a definition has an or inside one kind and can be said kind by kind, the verbalizer says it as one run of clauses joined by commas and or.
note: dropped the separate "for every definition_1" preamble sentence

ideal: It must be possible for a document to start with a refused frontmatter, for the checker to report that the document has a frontmatter it cannot read, and for some run to exit with code 2.
note: folded three existence clauses into one sentence

ideal:
For every document, unit, and word: when the document keeps no readings, holds the unit, and the unit declares the word, then none of these hold:
- a reading says the word and nothing declares it
- the word is declared in a unit that is not a term
- the word's reading is in another unit than its declaration
- no claim, definition or fact uses the word
- checker reports the word
note: restated each "is not a word that..." as a positive clause under "none of these hold"

ideal: For every unit: when it is unfounded, miscited, or circular, checker reports a finding for it.
note: combined three separate implications into one disjunctive antecedent

ideal: It must be possible for a bug that names an issue the tracker knows but has not closed, and that an expected failure checks, for the checker to report no finding for either the bug or the expected failure.
note: folded naming and tracking into one relative clause on the bug

ideal: For every word: when a unit declares it and no unit's claim, definition, or fact uses it, then it is a word that no claim, definition or fact uses.
note: tightened "there is no unit_1 such that..." to "no unit's claim... uses it"

ideal: For every unit and every word that is not a signature, checker does not report the unit's formula as lone on the word.
note: folded "when the word is not a signature" into the quantifier

ideal: Every unclosed frontmatter is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.
note: dropped the separate "for every / the X" sentence split

ideal: When the project has a runner, checker reports an untesting for every unguarded claim.
note: moved "for every claim" to scope only the unguarded condition

ideal: It must be possible for the verbalizer to fail on the formula of some unit with a fault of its own.
note: minor smoothing only

ideal: For every list: when it is a rule whose two sides are each one clause, whose first side does not begin with a time phrase, and whose second side does, the verbalizer says it with "then" before the time phrase.
note: merged three bullet conditions into one relative-clause sentence

ideal: For every document_1 and document_2: when document_1 is document_2 without its frontmatter, the two hold exactly the same units, and checker reports a finding for one exactly when it reports one for the other.
note: collapsed the two-way implications into "exactly the same" / "exactly when"

ideal: When the project has no tracker, checker reports no untracking for any unit.
note: moved "for every unit" since the condition doesn't depend on it

ideal:
All of these hold:
- when a unit is held with units that cannot all hold, checker names it in its report of a contradiction
- when a scenario cannot happen while every held unit holds, checker reports that it cannot happen.
note: dropped numbered variable subscripts, used "it"

ideal: When a frontmatter lists a missing plugin, checker reports that the project lacks it.
note: replaced repeated "the missing plugin" with "it"

ideal: For every document: when it starts with no listing frontmatter and the command line of a run does not name it, checker runs no plugin over it.
note: dropped the independent "for every plugin" quantifier, since the claim holds for all plugins at once

ideal: When a list is a rule whose first side begins with a time phrase, the verbalizer says it with "then" at the start of the second side, on a line of its own.
note: dropped "for every list" preamble

ideal: When a quantifier has several conditions, one of which begins with a time phrase, the verbalizer says it in full, with "there is" and the numbered name.
note: flattened the nested "when the following holds" into one clause

ideal: For every document and unit: when the document keeps readings, holds the unit, the unit holds a formula, and its statement is not current, checker reports the unit's statement.
note: used "its statement" instead of repeating "the statement of the unit"

ideal: Every misquoted frontmatter is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.
note: dropped the separate "for every / the X" sentence split

ideal: It must be possible for a unit that holds a formula and whose claim, definition, or fact uses a signature, for the checker not to report that formula as lone on the signature.
note: folded the "uses signature_1" condition into a relative clause on the unit

ideal: For every run that asks for a logic command: when checker reports no scenario as unable to happen and no unit as held with units that cannot all hold, the run exits with code 0.
note: folded "the run asks for the logic command" into the subject noun phrase

ideal: For every unit: when it holds a formula, has no statement, and its formula can be said in words, the statement is unwritten.
note: used "its formula" instead of repeating "the formula of the unit"

ideal: For every run and command: when the run asks for the command and the command is not available, checker reports it as an unknown command and the run exits with code 2.
note: replaced the repeated command name with "it" in the consequent

ideal: Every unterminated frontmatter is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.
note: dropped the separate "for every / the X" sentence split

ideal: For every quantifier: when its variable is the subject of the sentence and fits a noun phrase, the verbalizer says it with the noun phrase as the subject, such as "a tag names unit_1".
note: used "its variable" instead of repeating "quantifier_1 is a quantifier whose variable"

ideal: For every run that asks for the generate command and every unit whose formula cannot be said in words: checker says why it cannot be said, and the run does not exit with code 0.
note: folded "the run asks for..." into the subject noun phrase and used "it" for the formula

ideal: It must be possible for a definition to have an or inside one kind, with an alternative that does not begin with its kind.
note: merged the two bullet conditions into one noun phrase with "with"

ideal:
Always, both of these hold:
- for every owner and failing cleanup: when the cleanup runs on a disposed owner, the dispose of that owner has not thrown, now or at any later moment
- for every owner, its nearest error handler or boundary, and every failing cleanup: when the cleanup runs on the disposed owner, the cleanup's error has reached that handler, now or at some later moment.
note: pulled the shared outer "always" to the top instead of repeating it on each bullet

ideal: For every document_1 and document_2: when document_1 is document_2 without its frontmatter, checker reports a finding for one exactly when it reports one for the other.
note: combined the two-way implication into "exactly when"

ideal: Every foreign frontmatter is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.
note: dropped the separate "for every / the X" sentence split

ideal: When a document starts with a refused frontmatter, checker reports that the document has a frontmatter it cannot read.
note: merged "for every document and every refused frontmatter" into the "when" clause

ideal: When a quantifier's condition is not about its variable, the verbalizer says it in full, with "there is" and the numbered name.
note: dropped "for every quantifier_1" preamble

ideal: For every run: when some plugin returns code 2, the run exits with code 2; when some plugin returns code 1 and no plugin returns code 2, the run exits with code 1.
note: joined the two bullets with a semicolon into one sentence

ideal: When a conflict is hidden, checker reports a finding for it.
note: dropped "for every conflict" preamble, used "it"

ideal: When a scenario can happen while every held unit holds, checker does not report that it cannot happen.
note: dropped preamble, used "it"

ideal: When a list can be put in a sentence, the verbalizer says it in a sentence.
note: dropped preamble, used "it"

ideal: For every term and word, checker does not report the term's formula as lone on the word.
note: used "the term's formula" instead of "the formula of the term"
